site.name: Home, A–Z
placeholders: [YOUR OWN NOTE ABOUT WHY HOME MATTERS TO YOU]

chapters.title: Remembered
chapters.text: A crayon house, mama, papa and me. The first definitions of home are drawn by a child.

chapters.alt: Day 10 poster: Where? Where? with Everywhere and Nowhere houses
chapters.title: Address
chapters.text: Where? Everywhere? Nowhere? Home as a question with no zip code.

chapters.alt: Day 11 poster: a person inside a house made of flesh-colored pipes
chapters.title: Body
chapters.text: Home is a part of me. Walls made of arms, eyes and feet.

chapters.alt: Day 12 poster: four shells spelling HOME over a blue apartment facade
chapters.title: Shell
chapters.text: Every shell carries a home. Seven windows, seven stories.

entries.alt: Day 9 poster: red crayon house on blue paper
entries.def: 1. A triangle on top, a door, one watchful window, and smoke that curls like a doodle. 2. What home looks like before you learn perspective.

entries.alt: Day 9 poster: mama, me and papa drawn in crayon on yellow paper
entries.def: Mama, papa, me — drawn by how tall each one feels. The smallest figure is the only one standing in green.

entries.alt: Day 9 poster: a drawn bed with pillows on red paper
entries.def: The most honest room of the house: the place where you can say, out loud or not, that you don’t want to wake up.

entries.alt: Day 9 poster: a drawn TV with an antenna on green paper
entries.def: A glowing box with a wobbly antenna and two tiny dancers inside. Home is whatever plays your favorite thing.

entries.alt: Day 9 poster: a drawn green top and yellow shorts on pink paper
entries.def: What someone else picked for you each morning: a green top with a small heart, yellow shorts. Care, in the shape of clothes.

entries.alt: Day 10 poster: the words Your Address, Everywhere, Nowhere over a blue halftone house
entries.def: Where? Where? The line you write on forms until it stops sounding like a place at all.

entries.alt: Day 10 poster: Where? Where? with Everywhere and Nowhere houses
entries.def: Two answers to the same question. Home can be nowhere you can point to, and everywhere you stop long enough to be yourself.

entries.alt: Day 11 poster: a person standing inside a house built from flesh-colored pipes
entries.def: The first house you get, and the one you can’t move out of. Walls of arms, windows that are eyes, floors that are feet.

entries.alt: Day 12 poster: four colorful shells with letters spelling HOME
entries.def: A home that grows out of the one living in it. No two are alike, and none is ever left behind.

entries.alt: Day 12 poster: a grandmother leaning out of a shuttered window inside a shell
entries.def: The small frame where a life leans out: a grandmother, a couple, a cat, two dogs, a child on a mother’s arm.
